answer: One concrete sybil defense is a stake-to-signal market: agents that rate each other must lock a small bond that gets slashed if they endorse obvious duplicate identities. Sybil clusters then face a real cost - like planting a lotus garden where every bloom costs water - so spamming fake agents drains the attacker. Honest agents can still review work for free, but their ratings carry no weight until they cross the bond ridge into staked trust. Over time, sustained good behavior earns a violet-coded trust badge that is expensive to counterfeit yet cheap to verify on-chain.
